learn.hook: Hot sand, very little rain and camels walking slowly: welcome to the Thar Desert!
points: A desert is a dry place that gets very little rain. The Thar Desert is mostly in Rajasthan.
In a hot desert, days are very hot, but nights can be cold.
Many desert houses have thick mud walls and small windows, which keep the inside cool by day. In Kutch, Gujarat, round mud houses are called bhungas.
People save every drop of water. They collect rainwater in underground tanks and step-wells.
The camel is called the ship of the desert. Its wide, padded feet do not sink in sand, and its hump stores fat, not water.

example.q: Think it through: Why do people in the desert wear loose cotton clothes and turbans?
steps: The desert sun is very hot.
Loose cotton clothes let air flow and keep the body cool.
A turban or a covering protects the head from the hot sun and dusty winds.
example.answer: To stay cool and protect themselves from the hot sun and dust.

learn.reallife: If you visit Jaisalmer or Bikaner, look for thick-walled houses, camels and water tanks.

games.title: Desert facts

Deserts are dry and get very little rain.

Thick walls slow down the heat from getting inside.

quiz.q: Which animal is called the ship of the desert?
quiz.explain: Camels can walk long distances on hot sand, carrying people and loads like a ship on the sea.
quiz.mistake: Does not know why the camel is special in deserts

quiz.q: What does a camel's hump store?
quiz.explain: The hump stores fat. The camel can use it for energy when food is scarce.
quiz.mistake: Believes the common myth that the hump stores water

quiz.q: The Thar Desert is mostly in which state?
quiz.explain: Most of the Thar Desert lies in western Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where India's hot desert is

quiz.q: Why do desert houses have thick mud walls and small windows?
options: To let in more hot air
To keep the inside cool during hot days
quiz.explain: Thick walls and small windows stop the heat from coming in quickly.
quiz.mistake: Does not link house design with the weather

quiz.q: Why do the camel's wide, padded feet help in the desert?
options: They do not sink in soft sand
quiz.explain: Wide feet spread the camel's weight, so it can walk on soft sand without sinking.
quiz.mistake: Does not link body parts with the place an animal lives

quiz.q: How do people in the desert save water?
options: They collect rainwater in tanks and step-wells
They pour it on the road
quiz.explain: Since rain is rare, people store every drop in tanks and step-wells.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand water saving in dry places

quiz.q: What is a bhunga?
options: A round mud house in Kutch
quiz.explain: Bhungas are round houses with mud walls and cone-shaped roofs in Kutch, Gujarat.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the desert house of Kutch

quiz.q: Why can desert nights be cold after a very hot day?
options: The sun shines brighter at night
The sand loses its heat quickly after sunset
quiz.explain: Sand heats up fast in the sun and cools down fast after sunset.
quiz.mistake: Thinks deserts are hot all the time

teach.ask: Gappu landed in hot sand with no water around! How do people and camels live in the desert?
teach.praise: Well done! Deserts are hot and dry, so people save water, build thick-walled houses and use camels.
teach.nudge: What is the weather like in a desert, and how do people deal with so little water?

topics.title: Life in the hills and mountains

learn.hook: Snowy peaks, step-like fields and yaks with long hair: let us climb the Himalayas!
points: Hills and mountains are high lands. Places high up are cooler, and some get snow in winter.
Many houses in the hills have sloping roofs, so rain and snow slide off easily. They are often made of wood and stone.
On slopes, farmers cut flat steps into the hillside for farming. This is called terrace farming.
Apples grow in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir. Tea grows on the hills of Darjeeling and the Nilgiris.
People wear warm woollen clothes. In the high Himalayas, yaks give milk, wool and carry loads.

example.q: Think it through: Why do farmers in the hills make step-like fields?
steps: On a steep slope, rain water rushes down.
Rushing water washes away soil and seeds.
Flat steps slow the water and hold the soil.
example.answer: Flat steps stop the soil and water from rushing down the slope, so crops can grow.

learn.reallife: Look at pictures of Shimla, Gangtok or Munnar. Spot the sloping roofs and green step fields!

So that birds can sit on them
To keep the house hot in summer
quiz.explain: On a sloping roof, rain and snow slide down instead of piling up.

quiz.q: What is terrace farming?
options: Growing plants on a house terrace
Growing crops on step-like fields cut into hills
quiz.explain: In terrace farming, slopes are cut into flat steps so crops can grow.
quiz.mistake: Thinks terrace farming means farming on a rooftop

quiz.q: Which animal gives milk and wool and carries loads in the high Himalayas?
quiz.explain: Yaks have long thick hair and can live in very cold, high places.
quiz.mistake: Does not link animals with mountain life

quiz.q: Apples grow well in which state?

quiz.mistake: Does not know that apples need a cool climate

quiz.q: What kind of clothes do people in cold hills usually wear in winter?
quiz.explain: Woollen clothes keep the body warm in the cold.
quiz.mistake: Does not link clothes with the weather

quiz.q: Darjeeling and the Nilgiris are famous for growing…
quiz.explain: Tea plants grow well on the cool, rainy slopes of these hills.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the famous crop of these hills

quiz.q: As you go higher up a mountain, the air usually becomes…
quiz.explain: High places are cooler. That is why mountain tops can have snow.
quiz.mistake: Thinks being closer to the sun makes it hotter

quiz.q: Hill houses are often built with…
quiz.explain: Wood and stone are found nearby in the hills and make strong houses.
quiz.mistake: Does not link building materials with what is found locally

teach.ask: Gappu flew up a snowy mountain and his feathers are freezing! How do people live in the hills?
teach.praise: Great! Hill people build sloping roofs, farm on terraces and wear woollens. Gappu needs a sweater!
teach.nudge: What shape are hill roofs, and how do farmers grow crops on slopes?

learn.hook: Waves splash, boats sail out and coconut trees sway: let us visit the seaside!
points: The coast is land next to the sea. India has a long coastline on the west, the east and the south.
Coastal places are often warm and humid (damp air). Many get heavy rain in the monsoon.
Many people living on the coast catch fish, build boats, and grow coconut and rice.
Salt is made from sea water. The sea water is left in shallow pans, the sun dries it, and salt is left behind. Gujarat makes the most salt in India.
Kerala's backwaters are famous for houseboats. Many coastal houses have sloping roofs for the heavy rain.

example.q: Think it through: How does the sun help make salt from sea water?
steps: Sea water is let into shallow, flat pans.
The sun heats the water and it slowly dries up (evaporates).
The salt cannot dry up, so it is left behind as white crystals.
example.answer: The sun dries up the water, and the salt is left behind.

learn.reallife: Next time you add salt to your dal, remember it may have come from the sea and the sun!

games.title: Coastal life
items: Salt can be made from sea water.
The sun dries the water and leaves the salt behind.
Coconut trees grow well on many coasts of India.
Coconut trees like warm, wet places near the sea.
Coastal areas are always covered with snow.
Indian coasts are warm. Snow falls only on high mountains.
Fishing is an important job for many people on the coast.
The sea gives plenty of fish, so many families catch and sell fish.
Kerala's backwaters are famous for houseboats.
Houseboats float on the calm backwaters of Kerala.

quiz.q: What is the coast?
quiz.explain: The coast is the strip of land that meets the sea.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of coast

quiz.q: Which state makes the most salt in India?
quiz.explain: Gujarat, with its long coast and hot sun, makes most of India's salt.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where salt is made

quiz.q: What is the main job of many people living by the sea?
quiz.explain: The sea is full of fish, so fishing is a main job on the coast.
quiz.mistake: Does not link jobs with the place people live

quiz.q: Which tree grows in large numbers along the coasts of Kerala and Goa?
quiz.explain: Coconut trees grow well in warm, wet coastal places.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which trees grow on coasts

quiz.q: The weather on the coast is often warm and humid. What does humid mean?

quiz.explain: Humid air has a lot of water vapour in it, so it feels damp and sticky.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of humid

quiz.q: How is salt made from sea water?
options: The sun dries up the water and salt is left behind
quiz.explain: In salt pans, the sun dries the water away, leaving salt crystals.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand how salt is made

quiz.q: Houseboats on calm backwaters are a famous sight in which state?
quiz.explain: Kerala's backwaters are famous for their houseboats.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous sights of different states

quiz.q: Why do many coastal houses in Kerala have sloping roofs?
options: So that heavy rain water flows off quickly
quiz.explain: Kerala gets heavy monsoon rain, so sloping roofs let the water run off.
quiz.mistake: Does not link roof shape with heavy rain

teach.ask: Gappu is at the beach and sees boats and salt heaps. How do people live on the coast?
teach.praise: Splash! Coastal people catch fish, grow coconuts and make salt from sea water. Gappu loves the sea!
teach.nudge: What do people near the sea catch, and what do they make from sea water?

learn.hook: Why does a camel have long eyelashes, and why do some houses in Assam stand on stilts?
points: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years: hot or cold, wet or dry.
To adapt means to change our ways to suit the place we live in. People adapt their houses, clothes, food and work.
In parts of Assam that flood often, some houses are built on bamboo stilts so water can flow under them.
Animals adapt too: camels have long eyelashes to keep out sand, and yaks have thick long hair to stay warm.
Ladakh is a cold desert. It is very cold and dry, with little rain. Pashmina goats there grow very soft, warm wool.

example.q: Think it through: Why would a stilt house be useful in a place that floods?
steps: During floods, water rises over the ground.
A house on the ground would fill with water.
A house on tall stilts stays above the water.
example.answer: The house stays above the flood water, so the family and their things stay dry.

learn.reallife: Compare your clothes in summer and winter. You adapt to the weather too!

options: So that flood water flows under the house
quiz.explain: The stilts keep the house above the water during floods.
quiz.mistake: Does not link stilt houses with floods

quiz.q: How do a camel's long eyelashes help it?
options: They help it see in the dark
They keep sand out of its eyes
They keep it warm in snow
quiz.explain: In sandy winds, long eyelashes protect the camel's eyes.
quiz.mistake: Does not link body features with the place an animal lives

quiz.q: Ladakh is called a cold desert because…
options: it is very cold and gets very little rain
quiz.explain: A desert is a place with very little rain. Ladakh is dry and also very cold.

quiz.q: Which animal of Ladakh gives very soft, warm pashmina wool?

quiz.q: What is climate?
options: The weather for just one hour
The usual weather of a place over many years
quiz.explain: Weather changes daily, but climate is the usual pattern of a place over many years.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up weather and climate

quiz.q: Which of these would suit a person living in a hot, dry place?
quiz.explain: Loose cotton clothes let air flow and keep the body cool in the heat.
quiz.mistake: Does not match clothes with climate

quiz.q: How does a yak's thick, long hair help it?
options: It keeps the yak cool in the desert
It keeps the yak warm in the cold mountains
quiz.explain: Thick hair traps warmth, so the yak can live in freezing high places.
quiz.mistake: Does not link fur with keeping warm

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why houses and clothes look so different in Assam, Ladakh and Rajasthan. Can you explain?
teach.praise: Fantastic! People adapt their houses, clothes and food to suit the climate of their place.
teach.nudge: How does the weather of a place change the way people build houses and dress?
